outcomes: Each Gradle project, Android included, and each Maven module that packages code is a Putnami project, with an edge to each component it depends on in the same build, whether the build sits at the workspace root or in a subdirectory
putnami lint, test and build run the steps of the component's build, Gradle wrapper or Maven, in its directory, and a second run over an unchanged tree is a cache hit

A machine with no JDK, Gradle or Maven builds right after git clone: putnami install installs the pinned Eclipse Temurin JDKs the build asks for, through .java-version and its Gradle toolchains, its Gradle or Maven, each checked by SHA-256, and its dependencies, and each task installs what it still lacks
An Android build gets the Android SDK on a blank machine once the workspace's owner accepts its licenses in putnami.workspace.json, and a machine's own SDK stays in use
The test task reads the JUnit reports and the JaCoCo report the build writes into the test and coverage summary
A change to a lockfile reruns test and build, never lint
putnami test --test runs the tests a filter names, and a component in which it selects none passes; putnami lint also checks the documentation links
putnami serve and putnami run start an application, and putnami package and publish build and push its image
A component overrides any value of the Java profile in its putnami.json, and the override reaches the cache key
nonGoals: Comparing the Gradle wrapper's version with the machine: the wrapper downloads the version it names, and its properties file reaches the key
Gradle composite builds: an included build is part of the build that includes it
Android product flavors: a flavored app overrides the test step
Publishing a library to a Maven repository: Gradle or Maven publishes it
An application image for a build other than the Gradle application plugin and Spring Boot

A workspace-fetch that fills a dependency cache ahead of a hosted run without running repository code: resolving a Gradle build's dependencies evaluates its settings and build scripts, which run their plugins' code, through the repository's own wrapper jar, and Maven's dependency:go-offline loads the build's extensions and misses the dependencies a plugin resolves when it runs
Credentials for a private Maven or Gradle repository: the build reads its own settings
A deps-upgrade: a Gradle or Maven build moves its versions with its own tools
Running the Maven wrapper script mvnw: the release its properties name runs instead
Installing an Android SDK the workspace's owner did not accept the licenses of, or the platforms and build tools ahead of the Android Gradle plugin: it downloads the ones the build declares

text: The probe answers, for each candidate directory a Gradle or Maven build knows as a component: its name (the Gradle path without its first colon, ':' turned into '/', or the artifactId), its edges, the extension, the tag java, its type and metadata naming the build's reference, the variant, its stack root and the expected Java version.
A component is an application when its build applies the application or Spring Boot plugin, Android aside; any other is a library.
A Gradle build's root is the nearest directory with a settings file; a Maven build's root is the outermost pom.xml that lists the module, or the module's own.
It is its components' stack root, and an input-only project when it is no component.
A build inside another one, such as buildSrc, and a build file under a src, target or build directory are no builds of their own.
A directory both builds claim is the Gradle build's.
A Maven module is variant maven.
A Gradle project whose build file applies an Android plugin or holds an android block is android, or android-coverage with unit test coverage on;
one that applies java-platform is gradle-platform, version-catalog gradle-catalog;
any other is gradle, or gradle-jacoco when it applies jacoco.
A variant is a part of the profile applied before the project's override.
The toolchain check runs javac -version against .java-version, read up to its first character that is neither a digit nor a dot.

When javac is missing or outside it, the task installs under the Putnami home the Temurin JDK it accepts (8, 11, 17, 21 or 25, 21 first), checked by SHA-256, and runs it first on PATH and as JAVA_HOME. 8, 1.8 and 1.8.0 accept the 1.8.0_512 a Java 8 javac prints.
Offline, a task installs nothing.

Each Gradle step reads the Java majors the build's toolchains ask for: JavaLanguageVersion.of(N) and jvmToolchain(N), as a number, a string, a JavaVersion constant or a libs catalog version, in its build files, script plugins, buildSrc and build-logic, and the daemon JVM criteria.
For each major but the one running Gradle, it installs the pinned JDK, unless offline, and appends -Porg.gradle.java.installations.paths=<homes>.
A task or workspace-install of a Gradle build that applies the Android plugin keeps ANDROID_HOME, ANDROID_SDK_ROOT or sdk.dir in local.properties.

Else, when options["@putnami/java"].android.acceptSdkLicenses is true, it installs the pinned command-line tools by SHA-256, accepts the licenses with sdkmanager and sets ANDROID_HOME and ANDROID_SDK_ROOT.
Else an Android component's task fails naming the option.
Offline, it installs nothing.

A step that names {root}/gradlew in a build that has no wrapper, or gradle when none is on PATH, runs a pinned Gradle distribution installed under the Putnami home and checked by the SHA-256 services.gradle.org publishes: 9.8.2 on JDK 17 to 25, 8.14.6 on an older JDK.
Offline, a Gradle that is not installed fails the task.
The test filter reaches it as it reaches gradlew.

A step that names mvn runs the release the distributionUrl of .mvn/wrapper/maven-wrapper.properties names, whatever mvn is on PATH, installed under the Putnami home and checked against the distributionSha256Sum it states, else the SHA-512, then the SHA-256, its host publishes.
An archive with no checksum, another digest, or a URL that is not http or https or carries credentials is refused.
Without the file, the mvn on PATH runs, else Maven 3.9.11.

putnami install runs workspace-install at each stack root, in path order, except the projects disable.tags excludes: it installs the JDKs, then the build tool, then fills the dependency cache: an init script resolves every resolvable configuration of every Gradle project, one it cannot resolve whole being a warning and a build that does not configure an error, and Maven runs go-offline, best effort, with a warning that names what it misses.
Force refreshes the dependencies.

requirements.text: With offline dependencies, workspace-install installs no JDK, Gradle or Maven: a stack root whose JDK, Gradle wrapper distribution or Maven is missing is left out with a warning, and the dependency resolution runs with --offline, so it verifies what the caches hold.

After the toolchain check, a major such as 21 in .java-version matching every 21.x release, each task runs the variant's steps in the component's directory with no shell: the root's gradlew with the component's task path (check, test, assemble, their Android forms, or generateCatalogAsToml), or mvn --file {root}/pom.xml clean of the component alone, then --also-make verify for lint and test, package for build.

text: The test task reads the JUnit reports, build/test-results/test (testDebugUnitTest for Android) or target/surefire-reports, and the JaCoCo XML report into the test and coverage summary.
A component with no file under src/test expects no report.
A missing JaCoCo report is read as none, except for android-coverage, where it fails the task with stacks.report_missing.
test --test, short -t, runs the tests the filter names. gradlew or gradle gets --init-script <script> -Dputnami.testFilter=<filter>, global options after the last task;

the script, in the task's output, gives every test task the filter as --tests does, with failOnNoMatchingTests off. mvn, mvnw or mvnd gets -Dtest=<filter> -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false -DskipITs;
another program, none.
A component it selects no test in passes with zero tests.
The filter keys the task.

requirements.text: The java:lint selector answers the sources, the test sources the lint commands compile or check, the build files and the lint configurations, never the lockfiles: a lockfile change reruns test and build and keeps lint's key.

text: putnami serve builds an application's runnable form (installDist for the Gradle application plugin, the Spring Boot jar otherwise) under its stack root's lock, copies it aside, and runs the copy with the words of --args as its arguments and PORT and SERVER_PORT set to the port flag, until the user stops it;
it reports the server ready once the port accepts connections.
A library runs nothing.

requirements.text: putnami run builds the application's runnable form, runs it once with the args flag, and answers its exit code.

text: putnami package --docker assembles, with no Docker daemon, the OCI image of an application: its runnable form on the Eclipse Temurin JRE of its Java major, pinned by digest, or on a base the project pins by digest, run as a non-root user with PORT and SERVER_PORT set to the port flag, 8080 by default.
A library packages nothing.

requirements.text: putnami publish --docker pushes the packaged image through the shared publisher, and an application that publishes an image declares it as a member of the release set.

text: lint checks every relative link and anchor of the component's README.md files and doc/ trees with the SDK's documentation link check, a directory below it that holds a Gradle build, settings or Maven POM file answering for its own, and a broken one fails lint, unless the docs-links flag is false.
The check needs no JDK.
options["@putnami/java"] in a component's own putnami.json overrides its variant's profile: an object merges, any other value replaces the variant's whole.
The steps run and the files the java:<task> selectors answer follow the resolved profile, and putnami.json is an input of every task.
An unknown member, a change to id, markers or variants, or a stack-root input the manifest does not declare fails the task with stacks.project_config_invalid.

requirements.text: The manifest passes the stack core's conformance kit: its markers are the profile's, it lists the java:lint, java:test and java:build selectors, and each command runs one task that depends on the same task upstream, reads its selector and every variant's stack-root files for that task, and declares its command-output reports directory.
